title: Consumer Rights
description: Know your rights as a consumer when buying goods or services.

content.whatIsTheIssue: Every person who purchases goods or services is a consumer. Under Indian law, consumers are protected against unfair trade practices, defective products, deficient services, and misleading advertisements. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 strengthens these protections with provisions for e-commerce, product liability, and a central consumer authority.
yourBasicRights: Right to Safety — Protection against products or services that are hazardous to life and property
Right to Information — Right to be informed about the quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard, and price of goods or services
Right to Choose — Access to a variety of goods or services at competitive prices
Right to be Heard — Consumer interests will receive due consideration at appropriate forums
Right to Seek Redressal — Right to file complaints and get fair settlement of genuine grievances
Right to Consumer Education — Right to know about consumer rights and responsibilities
whatYouCanDo: File a complaint with the Consumer Forum (District, State, or National Commission depending on claim amount)
Use the online e-daakhil portal for filing complaints electronically
Complaints for goods/services up to ₹1 crore go to the District Commission
Contact the National Consumer Helpline (1800-11-4000) for guidance
Lodge complaints against misleading advertisements with CCPA
For e-commerce issues, file complaints directly with the e-commerce company first, then escalate

title: Cyber Safety Rights
description: Your rights related to online safety, privacy, and cyber crimes.

content.whatIsTheIssue: With increasing digital activity, citizens face threats like online fraud, identity theft, cyberbullying, and data breaches. The Information Technology Act, 2000 (and its amendments) provides legal protections against cyber crimes. Citizens have the right to privacy, safe digital transactions, and legal recourse against cyber crimes.
yourBasicRights: Right to Privacy — Your personal data is protected under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act
Right to report cyber crimes and get them investigated
Protection against identity theft, hacking, and unauthorized access
Right to compensation for data breaches by companies
Protection against cyberbullying and online harassment
Right to have intimate images removed from the internet (under IT Act Section 66E)
whatYouCanDo: Report cyber crimes on cybercrime.gov.in
Call 1930 for immediate cyber fraud assistance
File an FIR at any police station — cyber crime FIRs can be filed regardless of jurisdiction
Contact your bank within 3 days of unauthorized transaction for a better chance of recovery
Request data deletion from companies under data protection laws
Report social media harassment through platform reporting tools AND police complaint

title: Employment Rights
description: Know your rights as an employee — wages, safety, and fair treatment.

content.whatIsTheIssue: Employees in India are protected by various labor laws covering minimum wages, working hours, workplace safety, social security, and protection against unfair dismissal. Key legislation includes the Code on Wages, 2019, Industrial Relations Code, and the Occupational Safety, Health & Working Conditions Code.
yourBasicRights: Right to minimum wages as fixed by the government
Right to timely payment of wages — employers must pay within 7-10 days of the wage period
Right to equal pay for equal work regardless of gender
Right to a safe and healthy workplace
Right to form or join a trade union
Right to social security benefits (PF, ESI, gratuity)
Protection against unfair dismissal — notice period or compensation required
Right to maternity/paternity benefits
whatYouCanDo: File a complaint with the Labour Commissioner if wages are unpaid or below minimum wage
Lodge a complaint with the PF office if PF contributions are not being deposited
Contact the ESI office for ESI-related issues
File a complaint with the Sexual Harassment Committee (Internal Complaints Committee) at your workplace
Approach the Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal for wrongful termination
Use the UMANG app or EPFO portal to track your PF contributions

title: Women's Rights
description: Legal protections available for women regarding safety, equality, and justice.

content.whatIsTheIssue: Indian law provides comprehensive protections for women against domestic violence, workplace harassment, dowry, and other forms of discrimination. Key legislation includes the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, Dowry Prohibition Act, and various provisions of the Indian Penal Code.
yourBasicRights: Right to live with dignity and free from violence (Article 21)
Right to equal pay for equal work
Right to protection from domestic violence — right to reside in shared household
Right to file a complaint of sexual harassment at workplace (POSH Act)
Right to free legal aid
Right to file a Zero FIR (at any police station, regardless of jurisdiction)
Right to maternity benefits (26 weeks for first two children)
Right to maintenance from husband/partner
Right to education (Right to Education Act)
Right to property (equal inheritance rights under Hindu Succession Act amendments)
whatYouCanDo: Call Women Helpline: 181 for immediate assistance
Call Police: 112 in case of immediate danger
File a complaint under the Domestic Violence Act at the nearest police station
Approach the Internal Complaints Committee at your workplace for sexual harassment
Seek help from the National Commission for Women (NCW)
Access free legal aid through NALSA or State Legal Services Authority
File for maintenance under Section 125 CrPC in Magistrate's Court

title: Senior Citizen Rights
description: Legal protections and government benefits available for senior citizens.

content.whatIsTheIssue: The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 provides legal protections for senior citizens, including the right to maintenance from children and dependents, protection from abuse, and access to old-age homes. Senior citizens also have priority rights in property matters and legal proceedings.
yourBasicRights: Right to maintenance from children and relatives
Right to live in their own property — children cannot evict parents
Right to revoke property transfer if maintenance is not provided
Right to protection from abuse, neglect, and exploitation
Priority in court proceedings (cases involving senior citizens are expedited)
Right to free legal aid
Right to concessions in government services and travel
whatYouCanDo: File a maintenance claim before the Maintenance Tribunal (under the Senior Citizens Act)
Contact the Senior Citizen Helpline: 14567
Approach the Subdivision Magistrate or District Magistrate for maintenance orders
File a police complaint for abuse or neglect
Seek help from Senior Citizen Welfare Associations
Access free legal aid through NALSA

title: Student Rights
description: Know your rights as a student regarding education, fees, and campus safety.

content.whatIsTheIssue: Students in India are protected by the Right to Education Act, UGC regulations, and anti-ragging laws. Key issues include fee disputes, admission irregularities, ragging, unfair examination practices, and discrimination. Students have the right to quality education, safe campuses, and transparent evaluation.
yourBasicRights: Right to free and compulsory education (ages 6-14 under RTE Act)
Right to a safe campus free from ragging (UGC Anti-Ragging Regulations)
Right to transparent fee structure and no capitation fees
Right to fair examination and evaluation
Right against discrimination based on caste, religion, gender, or disability
Right to access scholarships and financial aid
Right to grievance redressal in educational institutions
whatYouCanDo: Report ragging: Call Anti-Ragging Helpline 1800-180-5522
File complaint on the UGC website for university-level issues
Approach the Fee Regulatory Committee for excessive fees
File RTI applications for information about your institution
Contact NCPCR for violations of the Right to Education
Approach the court for admission or examination-related issues

title: Tenant Rights
description: Your rights as a tenant — rent, eviction, deposits, and disputes.

content.whatIsTheIssue: Tenants in India are protected under various state Rent Control Acts and the Model Tenancy Act, 2021. Key issues include illegal eviction, excessive rent increases, security deposit disputes, and maintenance responsibilities. Both tenants and landlords have rights and obligations defined by the rental agreement and applicable state laws.
yourBasicRights: Right to a written rental agreement
Right to peaceful enjoyment of the rented property
Right against arbitrary eviction — landlord must follow legal process
Right to reasonable notice before eviction (usually 1-3 months)
Right to get security deposit back when vacating (minus legitimate deductions)
Right to essential services (water, electricity) — landlord cannot cut them off
Right to privacy — landlord cannot enter without notice
whatYouCanDo: Ensure you have a written rental agreement (registered if possible)
Document the property condition at move-in with photos
File a complaint with the Rent Authority/Controller for disputes
Approach the Civil Court for eviction-related matters
Contact the police if the landlord tries illegal eviction or cuts off services
Keep records of all rent payments (receipts or bank transfers)

title: Banking Rights
description: Your rights as a bank customer regarding accounts, loans, and services.

content.whatIsTheIssue: Bank customers in India are protected by the Banking Regulation Act, RBI guidelines, and the Banking Ombudsman Scheme. Key issues include unauthorized transactions, unfair lending practices, hidden charges, and poor customer service. Customers have the right to fair treatment, transparency, and grievance redressal.
yourBasicRights: Right to open a basic savings account (BSBD account) with zero balance
Right to be informed about all charges and fees
Right to compensation for delayed ECS/NEFT/RTGS transactions
Right to approach the Banking Ombudsman for unresolved complaints
Right to close your bank account without giving a reason
Right to refund for unauthorized electronic transactions (if reported within 3 days)
Right to not be forced to buy insurance or other products when taking a loan
Right to fair and transparent loan terms
whatYouCanDo: File a complaint with your bank's Grievance Redressal Officer first
If unresolved within 30 days, approach the RBI Banking Ombudsman
File complaints online on the CMS portal (cms.rbi.org.in)
For unauthorized transactions, report to bank within 3 days for zero liability
File an RTI application to get information from public sector banks
Approach the Consumer Forum for banking service deficiencies

title: Digital Rights
description: Your rights regarding personal data, online privacy, and digital services.

content.whatIsTheIssue: With increasing digitization, citizens have important rights regarding their personal data, online privacy, and access to digital services. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the IT Act provide legal frameworks for data protection, while the right to privacy has been recognized as a fundamental right by the Supreme Court.
yourBasicRights: Right to Privacy — recognized as a fundamental right (Puttaswamy judgment)
Right to know how your data is being collected and used
Right to consent before your personal data is processed
Right to access, correct, and erase your personal data
Right to data portability
Right to not be denied services for refusing unnecessary data collection
Right to access the internet and digital services
whatYouCanDo: Read privacy policies before sharing personal data
Opt out of unnecessary data collection by apps and websites
Request companies to delete your personal data
File complaints with the Data Protection Board when your data rights are violated
Report data breaches to CERT-In
Use privacy settings on social media and apps
Exercise your right to be forgotten where applicable

title: Police & Legal Rights
description: Your rights when dealing with police, during arrest, and in legal proceedings.

content.whatIsTheIssue: Citizens have fundamental rights when interacting with law enforcement, including the right to legal representation, protection against arbitrary arrest, and the right to a fair trial. Understanding these rights is crucial for protecting yourself and your family during police encounters.
yourBasicRights: Right to know the grounds of arrest (Article 22)
Right to consult a lawyer upon arrest
Right to be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest
Right against self-incrimination (Article 20)
Right to free legal aid if you cannot afford a lawyer (Article 39A)
Right to file a Zero FIR at any police station
Right to file an FIR — police cannot refuse to register an FIR for cognizable offenses
Right to a copy of the FIR
Women cannot be arrested after sunset and before sunrise (except in exceptional cases)
Right to bail (for bailable offenses, it's a right; for non-bailable, it's court's discretion)
whatYouCanDo: Demand to see the arrest warrant (for warrant-based arrests)
Contact a lawyer immediately upon arrest
Inform your family/friend about the arrest
Request a medical examination if subjected to police violence
File a complaint against police misconduct with the SP/DIG or Police Complaints Authority
Apply for bail before the Magistrate or Sessions Court
File a habeas corpus petition in High Court if illegally detained

title: Property Basics
description: Essential rights regarding property ownership, buying, selling, and disputes.

content.whatIsTheIssue: Property transactions in India involve complex legal requirements. Common issues include fraudulent property sales, boundary disputes, encroachment, title defects, and builder delays. The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA) provides protection for homebuyers, while property rights are governed by the Transfer of Property Act and Registration Act.
yourBasicRights: Right to own property (Article 300A — constitutional right)
Right to a registered sale deed for property transactions
Right to clear title — seller must provide clean title documents
Right to RERA protection when buying from builders (timely possession, quality, refund)
Right to compensation for delayed possession under RERA
Right to ancestral property (equal for sons and daughters under Hindu law)
Right against encroachment — legal remedies for encroachment on your property
whatYouCanDo: Always verify property title through legal search before purchasing
Register all property documents at the Sub-Registrar's office
File RERA complaints for builder-related issues (delayed possession, defects)
Approach Revenue Court for property boundary disputes
File a civil suit for property title disputes
Get an encumbrance certificate to verify no pending claims on property

title: Government Services
description: Your rights to access government services, RTI, and public welfare schemes.

content.whatIsTheIssue: Citizens have the right to access government services efficiently and transparently. The Right to Information Act allows citizens to seek information from public authorities. Various government schemes provide financial assistance, healthcare, education, and other benefits to eligible citizens.
yourBasicRights: Right to Information (RTI Act, 2005) — seek information from any public authority
Right to government services within specified timelines (state-specific guarantee laws)
Right to Aadhaar-linked services and benefits
Right to access public welfare schemes (PM-KISAN, Ayushman Bharat, etc.)
Right to public hearing (Jan Sunwai) for grievance redressal
Right to access birth/death certificates, caste certificates, and other documents
Right to access education (under Right to Education Act)
whatYouCanDo: File RTI applications online on rtionline.gov.in
Use UMANG app for accessing government services
Track your government scheme applications online
File complaints on CPGRAMS for central government grievances
Use DigiLocker for digital document management
Visit Common Service Centers (CSC) for government service access
Contact the relevant department's public grievance cell
